title: Return a calculated value
when: The question asks you to calculate and return a result.
use: double area = getArea(3, 4);
parts: Local copies of the caller’s inputs.
Send the result back to the caller.
change: Rename the function and parameters; replace the formula and result type.
watch: A non-void function must return a value on every normal path.

title: Change arguments using references
when: The function must change the caller’s variables.
use:
int x = 3, y = 8;
swapValues(x, y);
parts: An alias for the original variable; updates reach the caller.
Preserve the first value before overwriting it.
This function acts on arguments instead of returning a result.
change: Change int to double or another type; keep & when you want to modify the caller.
watch: Without &, you only swap local copies.

title: Default arguments and overloads
when: A call may omit an input, or use a different parameter type.
parts: Used when the second argument is omitted.
change: Change the default or calculations. If you add a prototype, put the default only there.
watch: Return type alone cannot distinguish overloads. Defaults belong on trailing parameters.

title: Declare first, define later
when: You need a prototype above main and the function body below main.
use: double result = average(3, 4);
parts: Announces the name, result type and parameter types.
Makes the arithmetic floating-point before addition and division.
change: Leave the prototype above main; move the definition below main if requested. Change the formula.
watch: Keep the declaration and definition types identical. Casting after integer division cannot restore the lost fraction.

title: Loop through an array
when: You need a total, search, count or other loop over values.
use:
double values[] = {2, 4, 6};
double total = sum(values, 3);
parts: Read the caller’s elements without modifying them.
Number of elements; the function cannot infer it from this parameter.
change: Replace the loop body with the operation required; remove const only if the function must change elements.
watch: Pass the real length. Do not use sizeof(values) here to find the array length.

title: Remember a value between calls
when: You need a ticket number or a running count.
use:
int first = nextTicket();
int second = nextTicket();
parts: Initialized once; its value survives later calls.
Increment the stored value before returning it.
change: Change the initial value or update rule.
watch: This is shared state for the function, not a fresh variable on each call.

title: Basic class: Rectangle
when: You need private data, constructors, getters, setters and a calculation.
parts: Data belongs to each object and is accessed through public methods.
Set starting values; their name matches the class and they have no return type.
Functions callers are allowed to use.
Promises the method will not change ordinary object fields.
The object’s field, distinguished from the same-named parameter.
change: Rename Rectangle everywhere, replace fields and constructor inputs, then replace the calculation. Add validation in setters if requested.
watch: End the class with };. Rectangle r(); declares a function; Rectangle r; constructs an object.

title: Methods outside a class
when: The question gives a class declaration and asks for definitions.
use:
Circle c(2);
double area = c.getArea();
parts: Says the definition belongs to Circle.
change: Put the class declaration in Circle.hpp with an include guard. Put definitions in Circle.cpp after #include "Circle.hpp"; compile Circle.cpp with main.cpp.
watch: Repeat const on the definition. Do not repeat a default argument on the definition.

title: Simple struct
when: You just need to group related values.
use:
Measurement m{12.5, 2.0};
m.value = 15;
parts: Each instance keeps its own value and time.
change: Rename the struct and fields; add other types as needed.
watch: Brace values follow the declared field order. Use a class with private fields when you need controlled access.

title: Static class member
when: You need one value shared by all instances.
use:
CircleS a(2), b(3);
int count = CircleS::getNumberOfObjects();
parts: One shared counter rather than a counter per object.
Provides storage and initial value once in a .cpp file.
Called with ClassName::; it has no this pointer.
change: Use the shared field for another class-wide quantity.
watch: This example counts calls to this constructor, not currently live objects; implicit copies are not counted. Do not put the outside definition in multiple .cpp files.

title: Base and derived class
when: You need a shared interface with different behavior for each shape.
parts: A pure virtual function: Shape is abstract.
The derived class uses Shape’s public interface.
Checks that this method matches a virtual base method.
An addition to the shortened lab pattern so deletion through Shape* is safe.
change: Rename the derived class and implement the required methods. Use Shape* when the concrete type can vary.
watch: You cannot instantiate Shape. This is a shortened lab adaptation: position fields and printMe are omitted.

title: Function template: maxValue
when: The same function should work with int, double or another comparable type.
use:
int a = maxValue(3, 8);
double b = maxValue<double>(3, 8.5);
parts: T is a type chosen when the function is used.
Both inputs and the result use that type.
change: Replace the comparison and body for the generic operation you need. typename and class are interchangeable here.
watch: The chosen type must support >. Mixed types may need an explicit <double>. Keep template definitions visible in a header.

title: Class template: BuildingG
when: Your class must store values of a caller-chosen type.
use:
BuildingG<double> b(2.5, 3.5, "Lab");
string name = b.getName();
parts: Only these fields vary with the chosen type.
Choose the type when creating an object.
Repeat template<typename T> and qualify with BuildingG<T>::.
change: Change the fields and operations to fit the question; keep all template definitions in the header.
watch: This course pattern expects T to accept 0 in the default constructor. Renaming the class also means renaming constructors and qualified definitions.

title: Derived class template
when: You need a generic class derived from another generic class.
use:
HouseG<double> h(3, 6, "Ada");
double x = h.getX();
parts: Pass the same chosen type to the base class.
Construct the base before initializing this class’s fields.
Access a member inherited from a dependent template base.
change: Rename the base/derived classes and replace owner with the extra data you need.
watch: A shortened BuildingG/HouseG adaptation; do not combine it with another definition of HouseG.

title: Pointer parameter and object access
when: A function receives an address and changes the pointed-to value.
parts: Reference to the pointer itself, so redirect changes the caller’s pointer.
change: Replace int with the required type. For an object pointer use p->method(); for an object use object.method().
watch: Do not dereference a null or dangling pointer. This code borrows addresses and does not delete them.

title: Allocate and return an array
when: The function creates an array whose lifetime must continue after it returns.
parts: Return the address of the first element.
The caller releases the returned allocation.
change: Change double to the element type and fill the array before returning it.
watch: size must be nonnegative. Never return a pointer to a local stack array. Pair new[] with delete[].

title: Objects, pointers and arrays
when: You need to create several objects and call their methods.
parts: An ordinary object; use a dot.
A pointer to an object; use an arrow.
Calls the default constructor for each element.
change: Replace Reading with your class. Use &readings[i] when a function expects a pointer to an element.
watch: Deleting the array destroys its objects. Do not delete p here: it points at a local object.

title: String methods and read-only reference
when: You need to find, split or examine text without copying the input unnecessarily.
use: string first = firstPart("Ada Lovelace");
parts: Read the caller’s string through a reference.
Returns a position, or npos when no match exists.
Copies pos characters starting at index zero.
change: Change the separator and substring positions. Use text.length() for its length.
watch: Check npos before using the result as a valid index. Use a string, not a string literal, to call string methods.

title: Read numbers from a file
when: You need to process every successfully read value.
parts: Input file stream; check opening before reading.
Run the body only after a successful read.
Distinguish the expected end of the file from other failure.
change: Change the input type and replace total += value with your processing. For whole lines use getline(input, line) and a string line.
watch: Do not loop on !input.eof(). Local streams close when they leave scope. The usage example creates a sample file.

title: Write or append a file
when: You need to save results without erasing earlier entries.
use: appendValue("results.txt", 12.5);
parts: Finish writing and check for failure.
change: Remove ios::app to replace the file contents. Change the output expression to write fields separated by spaces.
watch: Ordinary ofstream opening overwrites existing contents; choose the mode deliberately.

title: Throw and catch an exception
when: An invalid operation must be reported to the caller.
parts: Stop the current operation and transfer control to a matching handler.
Read the exception without slicing it.
change: Change the invalid condition and message; replace quotient with your own operation.
watch: Statements after a throw in the try block are skipped. An ordinary file-stream failure usually sets flags rather than throwing.

title: Singly linked list: IntSLList
when: You need to insert at either end and remove the head.
parts: info stores the integer; next links to the following node.
First and last node; both null when empty.
Update links, then update the relevant end pointer.
Save the value and node, update links, delete the old node, return the value.
change: Use the same pointer steps for other node data. Add traversal with for (IntSLLNode* p = head; p != nullptr; p = p->next) inside the class.
watch: deleteFromHead requires a nonempty list. Destructor frees nodes; copying is disabled to avoid shared raw ownership.

title: Lab 6 linked Stack<T>
when: You need LIFO: last in, first out.
parts: A node holds one item and the link below it.
The top node and the current item count.
Create a node, link to old top, move top, increment count.
Save the item, advance top, delete the old node, decrement count, return item.
Inspect without removing; empty access throws StackException.
change: Choose Stack<double>, Stack<string> or Stack<Shape*>. For Shape*, delete each owned shape after popping it; deleting nodes alone does not delete the pointed-to shapes.
watch: This uses the lab API: pop returns T. Keep template code in the header. Cleanup and disabled copying are practice additions.

title: Linked queue: ListQueue<T>
when: You need FIFO using the supplied list-based example.
parts: The standard list manages the linked nodes.
Read front, pop_front, then return the saved value.
Inspect the oldest item, test emptiness, or remove all items.
change: Choose the stored type with ListQueue<double> or another suitable type.
watch: Check isEmpty before front or dequeue. The supplied example uses list; use the linked-list template above to study manual node links.

title: Circular queue: ArrayQueue<T, size>
when: You need FIFO in a fixed-size array.
parts: Oldest and newest occupied indexes; -1 marks empty.
Check full, wrap last if needed, store the value.
Save the front value; reset if it was the last item, otherwise advance/wrap first.
change: Change <int, 4> to the item type and capacity you need. Keep the supplied first/last convention.
watch: Call dequeue only when nonempty. A full enqueue prints “Full queue.” and does not insert; it does not throw.
